summary.en-US: Watch YouTube at the exact speed you can follow. Go past the 2× limit, step by 0.1× where small changes matter, or set your own step sizes. Hotkeys, a player button, no tracking.

description.en-US:
YouTube's speed menu stops at 2×. If you watch lectures, conference talks, tutorials or podcasts sped up, you probably hit that ceiling a long time ago.

The jumps are too big, too. 1.75× drags. 2× works for one speaker and turns the next one into a blur. The speed you want is often something like 2.3×, and YouTube won't give it to you.

I built Granular Speed because 2× stopped being enough for me. Now I pick the exact speed for each video, and you can too.

**Out of the box**

- Up to 2×, the speed moves in 0.25× steps.
- Above 2×, it moves in 0.1× steps, up to 4×. That's the range where a small change decides whether you follow the speaker or lose them.
- Your speed sticks across videos, tabs and restarts. YouTube resets it on every new video and ad, and the extension sets it right back.

**Keyboard and mouse**

- Shift + . speeds up and Shift + , slows down. Those are YouTube's own speed keys, minus the 2× limit.
- R jumps between 1× and your last speed, for the part you want at normal pace.
- A speed button sits next to the subtitles button. Scroll over it, or click it for a slider and one-click presets.
- On Shorts, the button becomes a speed pill at the top of the video, so you always see where you are.

The keys work on any keyboard layout and stay out of the way while you type a comment.

**Make it yours**

It's called Granular for a reason. In the settings you choose:

- the step size below and above a switch point, as fine as 0.01×
- where that switch happens
- the slowest and fastest speed, anywhere between 0.1× and 16×
- up to 8 preset buttons

Learning a language or transcribing a solo? Set 0.05× steps below 1× and slow down without guessing. Firefox keeps voices at their natural pitch at every speed.

**Light and private**

There are no accounts and no analytics, and the extension never makes a network request. It stores your speed and your settings in your Firefox profile, nothing else. YouTube pages load about 16 KB of plain, readable code, and nothing runs in the background while you watch. The source is open on GitHub: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube

Not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

release_notes.en-US: First release on addons.mozilla.org. Speeds past YouTube's 2× limit, adjustable step sizes and range, hotkeys, a player button with a slider and presets, a speed pill on Shorts, and a settings page. Full history: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

version.approval_notes: No build step or minification: the submitted files are the source, also at https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube. To test, open any youtube.com/watch page and press Shift+. a few times, or click the speed button to the left of the subtitles button. The tune icon in that panel opens the settings page through background.js, which only calls runtime.openOptionsPage(). The toolbar button opens the same settings page.
